o: In the second season, the Harrigans struggle to show a unified front as rising rivals threaten their fractured criminal empire – and Harry Da Souza, their street-smart and formidable 'fixer', must walk a dangerous tightrope when tensions within the family intensify. As violence spills into every corner of their lives, loyalties snap, safety proves temporary, and the battle for power leaves no…

v.n: Tom Hardy Reveals How a Good Acting Performance Is Like…

eps.o: Maeve and Conrad go to the dogs, leaving Harry to deal with the messy fallout; Jan makes a startling confession; Kevin and Seraphina both look to the future; Tattersall puts his cards on the table.
With Conrad's self-control slipping, Maeve makes plans of her own while Jan hits Harry with a hard truth; smelling blood, Frankie and Tattersall circle like sharks.
Maeve probes Conrad for secrets, positioning herself against threats old and new. As Frankie forces a high-stakes sit-down, Kevin and Harry game out their strategy.

The Harrigans reel from an unexpected turn of events, triggering Harry to do damage control before police scrutiny closes in. Maeve's unseen hand moves Eddie out of London as Seraphina makes a new alliance and Conrad re-asserts his dominance.

Conrad declares war, stacking bodies and turning the Cotswolds into a fortress; Maeve plays puppet-master, sending Eddie on a mission before secrets start to spill, and a hit hurtles the Harrigans into all-out chaos.
Licking wounds and turning on each other after fleeing Frankie's assault, Seraphina goes all in, pitching the Harrigans on a global power play, while Maeve and Harry square off over crossed lines.

The Harrigans lock down the Cotswolds and roll back into London to shake the tree - buying loyalty with cash, threats and broken fingers; Maeve tightens the screws within the family, while Harry walks into a trap.
